set.body: The freeze rule forbids editing a published design doc; doc-verify --strict fails on a fabricated citation wherever it lives. Together they make the release gate permanently red — 48 fabrications sit in frozen dated design docs in this repo today, none of them correctable. Decide which condition the gate applies and make the gate passable without weakening it for documents that can still be fixed. Reported as GitHub issue #345.
set.title: doc-verify --strict is un-passable once a frozen doc carries a fabricated citation

set.resolution: doc-verify --strict now gates on editability, not freeze state: fabrication fails in a document that can still be fixed, and --staged keeps the gate on the commit that creates a frozen one. ADR-0009 records the decision and the two rejected alternatives.

set.body: The two new tests in TestStrictIsPassable call doc_verify.verify() in whatever directory the test runner stands in. verify() calls is_shallow() on that clone. The CI coverage job checks out shallow (no fetch-depth: 0), so every document short-circuits to the 'unresolvable' verdict before 'editable' is ever computed, and both assertions on 'editable' fail. Production behaviour is correct; only the tests depend on the ambient repo. Fix: build a throwaway repo like the sibling tests already do via RepoFixture.
set.title: Fix TestStrictIsPassable dependency on ambient git clone depth

set.body:
The Stop hook, hooks/stop-worklog-check.sh, runs every git command as 'git -C "$PWD"' and never calls 'git worktree list'. It asks two questions in one checkout: is the tree dirty outside .work/ and docs/roadmap.md, and is .work/todo.jsonl unchanged versus HEAD. If dirty is yes and the log is unchanged it concludes unrecorded work and blocks.

Worklog policy tells concurrent sessions to use a git worktree. Linked worktrees share one object store but each has its own working tree, its own branch, and its own .work/todo.jsonl. So the hook's two questions get answered by a checkout that is not the one the agent wrote to.

The false block: the session opens on the primary checkout, the agent records everything in a linked worktree, and the primary tree happens to be dirty for an unrelated reason. The hook sees dirty plus an unchanged primary log and blocks, though the work is fully recorded next door. The inverse also holds: a clean, fully logged worktree cannot satisfy a hook that never opens it. Copying events between trees by hand is forbidden, so there is no supported way to make the hook see the other log. The recommended concurrency model and the Stop check are at odds.

Fix: keep the dirty check at $PWD as the signal that work happened, but before blocking, walk 'git worktree list' and allow the stop if any checkout in the repo holds an uncommitted change to .work/todo.jsonl.

Known gap this fix does not close: the hook's proof of recording is an UNCOMMITTED change to todo.jsonl, so a session that records and then commits its items still reads as unrecorded. That gap exists in the single-checkout case too and needs a session-start marker to fix. Track it separately.
set.title: Stop hook accuses a correctly-logged worktree session of skipping the log

set.acceptance_criteria: A session that runs worklog add and then commits the log can stop without being blocked, proven by a test in tests/test_classifier.py that commits the todo.jsonl change before running the hook. The existing controls still pass: a session that recorded nothing anywhere is still blocked, and a stale marker from a previous session does not silence a genuinely unrecorded session. hooks/stop-worklog-check.sh and plugin/hooks/scripts/stop-worklog-check.sh stay byte-identical per tests/test_plugin.py.
set.body:
The Stop hook, hooks/stop-worklog-check.sh, treats an UNCOMMITTED change to
.work/todo.jsonl as its only proof that the session recorded its work. It runs
"git diff --quiet HEAD -- .work/todo.jsonl". A session that records its items
and then commits them leaves no diff against HEAD, so the hook reads a
correctly-logged session as an unrecorded one and blocks.

This is not the worktree bug fixed earlier. Widening the search to every linked
worktree does not help, because the committed log looks identical to a log that
was never written in every checkout. The gap is equally present in a single
checkout: record, commit, keep working, and the hook blocks on the next stop.

It bites the normal working rhythm hardest. Policy says record work first, then
do it, then commit. Any session that commits mid-flight and then touches another
file walks straight into a false block. The only ways out today are to stop
committing until the turn ends, or to answer the block with prose each time.

Proposed fix: give the hook a fixed point that does not move when the session
commits. SessionStart writes the HEAD sha to a session-scoped marker file. Stop
diffs .work/todo.jsonl against that recorded sha instead of against HEAD, so
events committed during the session still count as recorded. Keep the current
HEAD diff as the fallback when no marker exists, so a session that starts
without the SessionStart hook behaves exactly as it does now.

Check the interaction with the worktree walk already in the hook: the marker is
per session, the walk is per checkout, and the fix must not let a stale marker
from an old session silence a genuinely unrecorded one.
set.title: Stop hook cannot see work that was recorded and then committed
